$comment: Plugin SDK coverage matrix: the single source of truth. Edit this file, then run `php scripts/sdk-coverage.php` to regenerate docs/wiki/Plugin-SDK-Coverage.md. CI fails when sdk_version is behind Sdk::VERSION, when an SDK minor in the Sdk.php ledger is not named by any `since`, or when the generated page is stale. Security notes say only that a design is needed; vulnerabilities go through SECURITY.md, never here.

ratings.full: A plugin can read, change, react to and extend this area through a published SDK contract.
ratings.partial: Some of it is in the SDK; the rest is missing or reachable only through internal core classes.
ratings.none: No SDK contract. A plugin cannot interact with this area in a supported way.

areas.name: Users and accounts

has.what: user.creating, user.created, user.updated, user.deleted hook events
user.creating is read-only and can refuse an admin create with HookVetoException

missing: A user directory and membership reader
A supported way to provision or update users
Creation events on self-registration, invitation acceptance and SSO provisioning (only admin create fires them)
A slot on the user record page
areas.security: Hooks on account creation must not expose credentials or let a listener change the role. A read-only notification payload and a narrow, audited mutation contract are needed rather than more filter hooks.

areas.name: People directory
missing: A person read and search contract
areas.security: People records are personal data. A reader must be pinned to the current workspace, checked against relations:read for the caller, and able to redact fields.

areas.name: Sign-in, SSO and two-factor

has.what: ExternalAuthProvider and ExternalIdentity types (not yet wired to a registration path)

missing: Read-only sign-in, sign-out, two-factor and password-reset events
areas.security: An identity provider decides who an account belongs to. It needs a trust tier, operator-only enablement and binding per workspace. Sign-in events must be observe-only so no plugin can capture credentials or block sign-in.

areas.name: Workspaces

has.what: tenant.creating to tenant.deleted hook events
Veto a workspace deletion inside its transaction
Owned tables cascade on workspace deletion (PluginTablesInterface)

missing: A workspace read contract (name, plan, locale, enabled plugins)
areas.security: Install-wide plugins see every workspace's events. Hook subscriptions scoped to a workspace need a design before more workspace data is exposed.

areas.name: Roles and permissions

has.what: Route requiredPermission enforced by the host
PermissionResolver: read-only permission checks
Permission checks scoped to one record
Plugin-declared resource types
Role checks scoped to one record
ResourceScope: which records of a plugin resource type a caller may act on (narrowing only)
Declared permissions and seeded roles (PluginRolesInterface)
Role grants limited to the plugin's own permissions and roles, removed only by the plugin that made them

missing: Granting and revoking record-level roles through a contract
Events when a role's permissions change, and a veto on grants
areas.security: Anything that grants authority can escalate privilege. Role seeding and grants must be limited to the plugin's own roles and permissions, and every check must be bound to the caller's workspace by the host.

areas.name: Delegations
missing: Reading active delegations and the acting-for context
A veto on delegating a plugin-owned permission
areas.security: Delegation transfers authority, so plugins may observe and refuse it but must never create it.

areas.name: User groups and audiences

has.what: Plugin rule kinds in groups and routing (RoutingRuleResolverInterface)
Audience rule vocabulary shared with groups

missing: Resolving a group's or audience's members
areas.security: A plugin rule resolver returns people for a workspace. The host must drop anyone who is not an active member of that workspace rather than trusting the resolver.

has.what: ou.* hook events, including role assignment and a delete veto
Plugin OU types an admin adopts
ouScopePicker block

areas.name: Invitations and registration

has.what: membership.customer_joined when somebody joins a workspace through its own customer sign-up
Constants for registration.completed, registration.approved and registration.rejected

areas.security: A registration check may accept or reject, never set the role or unit, or it becomes an escalation path.

areas.name: Relations
areas.security: Relations hold family and guardian links. Writes need permission-checked contracts.

areas.name: Documents

has.what: documentViewer block
document.issuing (veto and checks), document.issued, document.rendered events
Issue documents as the person (Documents::issue)
Issue in the background where the workspace allows it
PluginDocumentStore, QR verification links and tracking
Document numbering rules and document.numbered
Preflight an issue without writing
document.revised
Issue in bulk from one template as a background job (Documents::issueMany)
Issue events for documents raised by form submissions
Published constants for document.routed and document.route_acted
route.sent_back, route.resubmitted, route.completed, route.signed and document.finalised events
Blocks a plugin adds to the document editor, drawn by Whity's renderer (documents.blocks, PluginDocumentBlocksInterface)

missing: Reading and listing documents other than the plugin's own
Withdraw and revise contracts, and document.withdrawn
Embed record providers and chart sources
areas.security: Document visibility depends on the caller and the route. A reader must apply the host's visibility policy per caller, and withdraw or revise must keep the audit trail intact.

areas.name: Templates, themes and the editor

has.what: Template slots in plugin.json
Template slots and merge-field providers for code plugins
Starter templates shipped by a plugin, seeded per workspace
Read published templates and their merge fields (Templates)

missing: Editor blocks, toolbar items and slash-menu entries
areas.security: Merge fields and editor blocks end up in printed, immutable documents. Providers must be held to the caller's workspace and permissions by the host, and plugin block markup needs a sandbox and server-side schema checks.

areas.name: Render service

has.what: DocumentRenderer, FlowDocument, PageSpec
Inline runs in flowing text
Render and issue from queue jobs and CLI commands

missing: Choosing a theme or brand when rendering
Rendering from a workspace template outside Documents::issue
areas.security: HTML or CSS input to the renderer would be an injection and server-side request surface. Keep input structured.

areas.name: Routing and approvals

has.what: Plugin routing rules that resolve recipients

missing: Reading a document's route and trail
Starting or acting on a route
route.completed, step-due events and a veto before an action
areas.security: Acting on a route is an approval on a person's behalf. It needs the actor bound by the host and the agent proposal policy.

areas.name: Plugin forms and public routes

has.what: form block and input blocks
Form preload from the plugin's own GET (dataSource)
Discriminated sub-forms (variant)
Anonymous form posts ('public' => 'form', PublicForm)
Anonymous link reads ('public' => 'read', PublicRead)

missing: Per-route rate limits beyond the host defaults

areas.name: Core forms and submissions

has.what: form.submitted, submission.reviewed and submission.withdrawn events

missing: Custom field types, validators and prefill sources
Mapping a submission to a plugin record
A slot in the form builder and in submission review
areas.security: Submissions hold personal data and anonymous input. Readers must respect member and reviewer scope, events should carry ids only, and a plugin field type on a public form needs the same gate public forms already have.

areas.name: Meetings and decisions
missing: Agenda-item sources and a minutes slot
areas.security: Attendance, quorum and decisions are legal facts. Writes need a host-bound actor and audit.

areas.name: Inbox and Waiting for you

has.what: inbox and timeline blocks for the plugin's own items
Inbox source contract (InboxSource, KeysetInboxSource, PluginInboxSourcesInterface): plugin sources reach the merged inbox, urgent first then newest, paged by position

missing: Acting on an inbox item from a plugin
areas.security: Each source must answer only for the caller in the current workspace. The host has to enforce that rather than trust the source.

areas.name: Time windows

has.what: Plugin window types an admin adopts

missing: Resolving a date to its window
A closed-period guard for plugin records
areas.security: A closed period is a bookkeeping rule. Writes into it need a host-enforced guard.

areas.name: Workspace records and automations

has.what: plugin.json manifest
Manifest expressions
Record types
Record rules, defaults, computed and locked fields
Automations
Manifest tests
issue_document automation step

missing: send_webhook, ask_approval, wait and call_action steps
Triggers from core events (form submitted, document issued)
areas.security: Triggers from another area's events must carry ids and re-read under the run's permissions. send_webhook needs an egress allowlist.

areas.name: Data types

has.what: Plugin-owned data types with generic admin screens
Lifecycle writes and guards

missing: Data types as document merge fields

areas.name: Reports
areas.security: A report aggregates across records, so row visibility per caller must be enforced by the host or totals leak across units.

areas.name: Search and the command palette

has.what: Data types that declare search are found by /api/search

areas.security: Results must be filtered by what the caller can see. The declarative path is safe; a free-form source needs host-side scoping.

areas.name: Settings

has.what: Declared, typed, namespaced settings keys
Read and write the plugin's own keys in the current workspace, and a settings-changed event

missing: A settings page per plugin and per workspace

areas.name: Secrets

has.what: PluginSecrets: encrypted per plugin and workspace
A host-rendered secret entry field that never returns the value

areas.security: The host, not the caller, must decide which plugin and workspace a store belongs to.

areas.name: File storage

has.what: Multipart uploads
PluginFiles and ready-made file routes

areas.security: The host must decide which plugin and workspace a store belongs to.

has.what: NotificationTransport contract (not yet discovered from plugins)
A Notifier service: send to a person, role or unit in the current workspace
Declared notification types with English and Arabic labels
WorkspaceEmails host service: send an email as the workspace (its brand, language and the EM.1 layout) to anyone, such as a customer's invoice; plain text only, one button, best effort

BillingEmails host service: Whity's own email about a workspace's plan, in the instance's brand to its billing:pay members; only for a plugin that declares PluginBillingEmailsInterface and the operator granted, capped per workspace a day

areas.name: Messages and channels

has.what: MessageChannel contract and PluginMessageChannelsInterface: add a channel such as WhatsApp or SMS (send, receive with the channel verifying the provider, delivery status, capabilities, templates)
Messaging\CustomerMessages host service: tell a workspace's customer something through Messages, trying channels in the plugin's order (WhatsApp, then email)

missing: A host service for a plugin to read conversations
areas.security: A channel must verify every inbound request itself and act only for the workspace it is called for. The host never parses provider payloads and namespaces every plugin channel.

areas.name: Languages and translations

has.what: English and Arabic labels on settings, data types, manifest screens and agents
The request's language on the SDK Request
Translatable content fields, shown by language on CRUD screens

missing: Arabic labels on frontend features, navigation and block text

areas.name: Branding and themes

has.what: Theme token override from a plugin route

missing: Choosing which plugin's override applies per workspace
areas.security: The theme route is public and runs on every page. Per-workspace overrides need a design.

areas.name: Navigation

has.what: Frontend features become sidebar items; navigation.register hook

missing: Top bar, user menu and create quick actions
areas.security: Navigation listeners receive the whole menu. Contributions should be append-only with links checked as internal paths.

areas.name: Home page

has.what: One home card per plugin

missing: More than one card, and actions on cards

has.what: Declared audited plugin events
timeline block
Recording an entry with a target, attributed by the host
Reading the plugin's own audit entries
Plugin job handlers
Enqueueing the plugin's own jobs in the current workspace
Scheduled (cron) jobs, run once per workspace
Status of the plugin's own jobs
Plugin health probes on the status page

areas.name: Plans, entitlements and payments

has.what: Declared sellable limits in the plan catalogue (PluginEntitlementsInterface)
Selling store plugin licences through one billing plugin (LicenceSales, PluginLicenceSalesInterface)
Asking the host to re-read a workspace's billing access (AccessRefresh)
Read-only plan prices (PlanCatalogue)
Read-only plan prices (PlanCatalogue)
Asking the host to re-read a workspace's billing access (AccessRefresh)
A plugin can be the deployment's billing portal: checkout, subscriptions, customer portal, refunds and verified provider notifications (PluginBillingPortalInterface)
Whether a paid Whity store plugin is licensed here: licensed, grace with an until date, or unlicensed, from the store's signed statement with a 7-day offline window (Licensing\StoreLicence)

missing: Reading entitlements and consuming meters through the SDK
areas.security: Charging moves money. It needs consent, the ledger, idempotency and webhook trust; meters must stay bound to the workspace.

areas.name: Install, versions and lifecycle

has.what: SDK version constraint
Core version constraint

missing: Knowing whether the plugin is on for the current workspace
areas.security: Installing and enabling stay operator-only. A lifecycle callback must not let a plugin enable others.

areas.name: Logging, errors and rate limits
missing: Reporting errors to the error tracker
areas.security: Plugin payloads must pass through the same scrubber before they reach logs or the error tracker.

areas.name: Database and migrations

has.what: Migrations
Tenant-isolation conformance kit
SchemaInspector
Upsert and SequenceAllocator
Undeclared-reference linter
Offline-host conformance kit

missing: A runtime connection handle from the SDK
areas.security: Workspace isolation is checked by lint and tests, not enforced. A connection bound to the workspace is a design question.

has.what: Request and Response
Multipart requests
Service routes: server-to-server calls with the trusted issuer's token, and the people they name (ServiceCall, LinkedPeople)
Route schemas in the OpenAPI document
Workspace, language and actor kind on Request

areas.name: Hook events

has.what: Events catalogue
Veto exception
Observe-only listeners, a list of what each event lets a listener change, and constants for events core already fired

missing: Published constants for document.routed and document.route_acted
Events for settings, plugins, plans, notifications, files and jobs

areas.name: Command line
areas.security: Commands run with full database rights outside RBAC. A plugin command must be operator-only and name its workspace explicitly.

areas.name: Personal preferences
missing: Reading the person's language, calendar and density

areas.name: Plugin screens and blocks

has.what: Frontend features (crud, action, custom)
Server-driven blocks
Data blocks
chart block
Sort, filter and paging
Embedded screens
dataRecord and recordFields blocks
visibleWhen and accessGate
flow block
Labels and other visible text in English and Arabic ({en, ar}), served in the reader's language

missing: Native screens for store plugins (custom screens need a change in this repository)
areas.security: Embedded screens are not isolated from the app. Third-party UI needs a separate origin, a message bridge and a scoped token first.

areas.name: Slots in core screens
missing: Tabs, sections and actions on person, user, role, unit, workspace and document record pages
Slots in admin screens, settings and the person's own settings
Top bar and user menu entries
areas.security: A slot receives the record it sits on. It needs per-record permission checks and the same own-routes rule blocks have.

areas.name: Desktop app

has.what: Plugins run under the offline desktop PHP host

missing: Rendering plugin blocks in the desktop or Flutter apps

has.what: Plugin routes become MCP tools
Hand-authored tools
Tool annotations
Tool context
Toolsets, visibility, agent policy and undo windows
Caller identity: person, agent or system
The host decides whether a tool only reads
Previews of what a proposed tool call would change
Plugin prompts
Plugin resources, read with the caller's context
Prompts and resources only from plugins the operator granted agent context, each gated by permission
Agent presets
Plugin agents
Agents service: the workspace's agents and their activity, as the calling person
Agent lifecycle events
MCP connections, read without secrets, and connection events
agentPolicy propose and suggest-only on plugin tools
Proposal created, decided and undone events
Plugin-provided previews of a proposal, run read-only

areas.name: Outbound webhooks and connectors
missing: Subscribing external URLs to events, with signing, retries and a delivery log
areas.security: Outbound calls need a guard against private addresses, signing secrets kept in PluginSecrets, a workspace check per event and id-only payloads.

areas.name: Calendar and bookings

has.what: Booking payment step (PluginBookingPaymentInterface, Calendar\BookingPaymentStep): require a payment such as a deposit before a booking is confirmed; core holds the slot as pending_payment and the plugin settles it through the Calendar\Bookings host service
Busy times from outside core (PluginCalendarBusyInterface): read when free times are listed and again inside the lock before a booking is written; failures fail open
Calendar\CalendarEvents host service: keep events from an outside calendar on a person's calendar, keyed by the plugin's own reference
calendar.event.created|updated|deleted and booking.created|confirmed|rescheduled|cancelled|expired events with ids only

missing: Reading a person's bookings and services from a plugin
A slot on the booking page for plugin fields
areas.security: A payment step and a sync plugin act only for the workspace they are called for, through host services that re-apply it; they never write calendar tables. Core never takes card details.
